plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant, delicate blossoms open on bare branches while winter still grips the landscape. Each flower has five rounded petals and gives off a sweet, spicy perfume. Ume groves are a beloved sign that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, with peak bloom often in February
plants.location: Japan, including Atami and Mito, and across East Asia
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. The fruit is pickled into umeboshi and steeped into plum wine.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with golden stamens at the center. They brighten gardens in the cool, damp months of late winter. Whole petals often drop in one piece, leaving a carpet of color beneath the plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with peak bloom from January to March
plants.location: Gardens of the southeastern United States, Japan, and Mediterranean Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative of this plant, produces all the world's true tea.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding white bells with green-tipped inner petals push up through frost and sometimes snow. They form drifts across woodlands and old churchyards. Their appearance is a quiet signal that winter is loosening its hold.
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them survive cold. They also yield galantamine, a compound used in medicine.
